source.ref: owner ask 2026-09-23, four instructions against the live console

patch.detail:
OWNER ASK 2026-09-23, four instructions, verbatim: "2. Condense all sorting and controls into an intuitive header bar. 3. Force the calendar to fill the full bottom right content space. 4. Make calendar scroll vertical. 5. Make the Ask Vera box more prominent with a tool tip prompt in the suggested text." (Instruction 1, the blink, is LIVE-477 and LIVE-481 and is not this row.)

2. ONE HEADER BAR. The console header carried the month, the zone, Prev/Today/Next, the four-panel toggle, Pencil it in, the shortcut sheet and Close, and then the grid UNDER it drew two more bands of its own: a slim strip with the month-and-year jump and the grid/list switcher, and below that the row of layer chips (Events, In the works, Private, Unavailable, To-dos). Two headers, one on top of the other, split by where the control happened to be implemented rather than by what it does. All five are in the console header now, grouped by job: WHEN (the month, which is the button that opens the jump, the zone, Prev/Today/Next), WHAT (the layer chips), HOW (the grid/list switcher), ACTIONS (Guest preview and the four-panel toggle, Pencil it in, the shortcut sheet, Close behind its own divider). The switcher and the chips are shown only on a panel that has them to offer: List and Workflow get neither, the Guest preview gets no chips.

THE TRAP THIS ROW HAD TO WALK PAST, AND THE GATE IT LEAVES BEHIND. LIVE-475 exists because the first cut of `hostChrome` took the switcher and the jump off the grid while NOTHING drew them: switch the page grid to List, press Fullscreen, and you were in list mode inside a full-screen console with no way back to the month and no way to move more than one month, with closing the console the only exit. That was fixed by keeping both inside the grid, which was right while no host drew them and is exactly what this row changes. So the rule is restated in the form that generalises, and made measurable: `calendarChrome()` says what comes off, `HOST_DRAWN_CONTROL_MARKS` names the `data-calendar-console-*` marker the host must carry for each one, and the probes on this row, on LIVE-474 and on LIVE-478 all fail the build if the grid gives up a control whose marker is not in components/spaces/calendar-console.tsx. A host may only take a control it actually draws.

The switcher, the chips and the jump panel moved to components/events/calendar-chrome.tsx and are rendered from BOTH sites, because a control written out twice drifts and a drifted control is the dead end again with more steps. Their state moved into CalendarWorkspace the way `month` already had, since a control drawn outside the grid cannot hold state that lives inside it; the grid takes `view` / `onViewChange` and `hiddenLayers` / `onHiddenLayersChange` exactly as it already took `month` / `onMonthChange`, and on the page, where nothing else draws them, it keeps drawing and holding both itself.

3. THE MONTH FILLS THE STAGE, AND THE REASON IT DID NOT IS ONE WORD. PROG-CAL13 had already made the console a fixed-height grid with the stage row at `minmax(0,1fr)`, given the grid `fill`, and taken the floor off the cell, so the tracks were right. What was wrong was the panel slider: it carried `min-h-full`. A single-line flex container only hands its own cross size to its line when that cross size is DEFINITE, and a `min-height` is not one, so the line was sized to the tallest item instead. `self-stretch` on the showing panel then stretched it to its own content, and the `h-full` under it had no definite parent to resolve against. The month drew at its natural height and the rest of the stage was empty under it. `h-full` in the console makes the cross size definite and the whole chain resolves. A panel taller than the console (a long List index) still overflows and the wrapper above it scrolls, vertically. The two bands of chrome removed in instruction 2 are the rest of the height back.

4. VERTICAL IS THE AXIS, read as: vertical is how you move through the calendar, and nothing in the stage moves sideways. What was already true stays: Up and Down page the month and the wheel pages it, `verticalScrollTaker` gives the key or the wheel to anything under it that can still scroll (a busy day scrolls inside its own cell, the agenda scrolls itself), and a sideways touch swipe keeps paging months because the owner ruled that in with PROG-CAL12 and a swipe is not a scroller. What changed: the stage itself now carries `overflow-x-hidden`, stated at the console boundary rather than left to whichever child happened to have it, so a panel added later cannot quietly introduce a second axis. NOTHING WAS FOUND SCROLLING SIDEWAYS IN THE STAGE TODAY: the panel slider was already clipped by its wrapper and the Workflow board is a responsive grid, not a carousel. This half of the instruction is a contract made explicit and measurable rather than a bug removed, and that is recorded here rather than claimed as a fix.

5. ASK VERA. The box keeps the foot of the side bar the owner asked for. It carries its own tint and a real elevation now, its cap in the console is a little higher so the ask, its Send and the suggestions are all on screen, and the suggested text is the part that changed most. It used to summarise itself as "Pencil, move or retitle in plain words", which names three verbs and teaches none of them. The closed row now shows a real ask with the tooltip that says what Vera would come back with, and opening the box offers the whole set as chips, each named by its own words, each carrying that sentence as its `title`, and each FILLING the field rather than sending it, so a person still reads what they are about to ask and can change a word first. The list is `VERA_SUGGESTIONS` in lib/calendar/vera-command.ts, beside the change kinds it maps to, one per shape the box can actually apply, so a suggestion cannot drift into something Vera cannot do. Undo is deliberately NOT one of them: it is the Undo control in "What Vera changed" (PROG-CAL11 slice 3) and not a sentence `parseVeraChange` accepts, so the box says where it lives instead of teaching an ask that would come back as a clarification.

WHAT ONLY A BROWSER CAN PROVE. The fill is a CSS layout consequence and jsdom has no layout, so the suite pins the CLASSES that decide it (`h-full` on the slider, `flex-1 min-h-0` on the grid, `overflow-x-hidden` on the stage) and the reasoning is at the site. Whether 1440x900 now shows six full week rows is a real-browser reading and is not claimed here.2026-11-27 (SCAN-1344): the public Calendar tab stopped carrying its own team mode, per the owner ruling of 2026-11-25 ("Public only, link to team"). The team half of this row now lives on the team calendar at /spaces/<slug>/settings/calendar; the probe was rewritten to measure that.

2026-11-27 (SCAN-1344 follow-up): components/spaces/calendar-console.tsx was removed with the rest of the public tab's retired team mode; source re-pointed to the tab.
